Consult Summary:
- Telemedicine consult for worsening widespread eczema over several days with intense pruritus and dryness; no systemic symptoms; plan includes continuing emollients, initiating fexofenadine, and escalating to topical Betnovate twice daily with 2-week follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sore, red, very itchy, and dry skin.
- Distribution: Chest, hands, arms; worst in the antecubital fossae (inside elbows).
- Timeline: Onset over the past few days; getting “way worse.”
- Character: Dryness; cracked areas present; denies weeping/oozing. No visible scratch marks reported. Denies thickened/darkened skin.
- Associated symptoms: Denies fever/temperature and joint pains. Feels otherwise well.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not discussed.
- Prior/Current management:
  - Emollients: Diprobase cream; “Dermal/Dermol” shower product—used daily without change.
  - Topical steroid: Over-the-counter hydrocortisone previously tried; not helpful.
  - Antihistamines: Previously tried an OTC option (clinician suggested cetirizine); patient reports it did not help. Not currently taking antihistamines.

Past Medical History:
- Atopic dermatitis (eczema): Recurrent; current flare is more extensive than usual.
- Asthma: Uses “blue inhaler” as needed during flares; not daily. Breathing currently OK.
  - Medications associated with asthma: Short-acting bronchodilator (“blue inhaler”)—dose/route/frequency not documented.

Social History:
- Not discussed (no data on tobacco, alcohol, substance use, occupation, or living situation).

Family History:
- Mother: Migraine.
- Thyroid disease in mother: Patient stated hypothyroidism; clinician repeated “hyperthyroidism” (conflict noted).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Medications (as discussed):
- Diprobase emollient cream (topical) – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- “Dermal/Dermol” shower product (topical wash) – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Hydrocortisone topical (OTC) – recent trial; not helpful; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Blue inhaler for asthma (short-acting bronchodilator) – as needed; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Newly prescribed: Fexofenadine (oral antihistamine) – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Newly prescribed: Betnovate (topical corticosteroid) – apply small amounts; instructed twice daily for the next couple of weeks.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals documented.
- No physical examination findings documented (telemedicine consultation).

Investigations:
- None ordered or reviewed.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Widespread eczema flare (atopic dermatitis), worsening over days; pruritic, dry, with cracks; no weeping; no systemic symptoms.
  - Plan:
    - Start fexofenadine (oral antihistamine); dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Escalate topical steroid to Betnovate (topical): apply small amounts (fingertip unit guidance provided) twice daily for approximately 2 weeks.
    - Continue regular emollients: Diprobase cream and Dermol/Dermal soap substitute.
    - Education: Use very small amounts of steroid as instructed; monitor for adverse or allergic reactions (unlikely but possible).
    - Follow-up: If worsening occurs, contact clinic earlier; otherwise reassess in ~2 weeks. If no improvement, return for further evaluation.
    - Prescription logistics: Sent to Boots pharmacy for collection.
- Issue 2: Asthma, currently stable; uses blue inhaler PRN during flares.
  - Plan:
    - Continue PRN use of blue inhaler as needed. No acute concerns noted during this visit.

General plan items:
- Return/call if symptoms worsen, no improvement after 2 weeks, or any adverse reaction occurs.
- Maintain skin care regimen as directed.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Vital signs and in-person skin examination findings.
  - Complete medication reconciliation with doses, routes, and frequencies (fexofenadine dose/frequency not documented; Betnovate strength not documented; hydrocortisone specifics not documented; blue inhaler specifics not documented).
  - Allergy verification beyond medications (e.g., latex, foods) not documented.
  - Social history (tobacco/alcohol/substance use, occupation) not documented.
  - Trigger assessment (soaps, detergents, stress, temperature, recent illness, new products) not documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Family history: Patient reported maternal hypothyroidism; clinician restated as hyperthyroidism (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Several incomplete/inaudible segments; product names partially unclear (“Dermal/Dermol,” “Betnovate” referenced). Clinical intent was generally clear.
